figures.prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: 16:9 editorial science review cover, wide 1536 by 864 composition. Create an original refined conceptual illustration about why equally flat electronic bands can support different collective order. Two equally thin perfectly level rectangular translucent enamel-glass planes float side by side at exactly the same elevation, seen from a shallow oblique angle. Their outer shapes and flatness are identical. Within the left plane, subtle silver-blue sinuous closed contours overlap and extend across the whole plane, suggesting distributed correlations. Within the right plane, warm amber patches repeat in a sparse orderly spatial pattern, suggesting translation-breaking density order. Keep both surfaces equally flat, with no mountains or energy slope. The internal marks are abstract, not literal atomic sites or actual wavefunctions. Restrained sculptural glass/enamel relief, midnight blue background, luminous ivory edges, muted ice blue and amber, soft raking light, delicate frosted texture, strong negative space and visually balanced tension. The two patterns must remain legible as small thumbnails. No arrows, chart axes, numerals, text, labels, logos, devices, qubits, molecular ball-and-stick, circuit boards, brains, cosmic stars. This is an interpretive conceptual cover, not measured data, not a material structure or demonstration of anyon braiding.
figures.caption_ko: 같은 높이의 평평한 두 판 안에 서로 다른 무늬를 배치해, 작은 밴드폭만으로 다체 질서가 정해지지 않음을 상징한다. 실제 재료 구조·파동함수·계산 데이터가 아닌 AI 생성 개념 그림.
figures.caption_en: Equally flat planes contain different internal patterns, symbolizing that a small bandwidth does not determine many-body order. AI-generated conceptual illustration, not a material structure, wavefunction or calculated dataset.
figures.alt_ko: 같은 높이에 놓인 두 얇은 평면. 왼쪽에는 넓게 겹친 곡선, 오른쪽에는 규칙적으로 반복되는 밝은 패치가 보인다.
figures.alt_en: Two equally thin flat planes at the same elevation, with overlapping extended contours on the left and regularly repeated bright patches on the right.
